A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LVLM-Count work. Their text, tables, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained and relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original counting experiments across four benchmarks, component ablations, accuracy analyses, qualitative examples, and inference-time measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds TallyQA-Complex evaluation, parsing-failure measurements, zero-count analyses, and a two-axis division experiment.

M1.justification: Appendix S introduces and evaluates a variant using horizontal as well as vertical divisions, extending v3's vertical-only procedure. The main four-stage pipeline remains unchanged. Newly documented parsing and prompting details do not independently establish changes to the earlier implementation.

E1.justification: Appendix T adds actual evaluation on TallyQA-Complex, extending quantitative coverage to real-scene questions involving relationships, attributes, and reasoning. v3 used TallyQA only for an answer-distribution analysis. The four original counting benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The timing comparison in Table 13 expands from GPT-4o to include Gemma 3 and Qwen2 baseline/pipeline pairs. GroundingREC, CountGD, DAVEprm, and TFOC in the expanded main accuracy tables were already evaluated in v3's Appendix K; their redisplay does not introduce new accuracy comparators.

E3.justification: The new TallyQA-Complex evaluation samples up to ten questions per ground-truth count, producing 149 questions, and specifies REC-8K-trained GroundingREC weights. New diagnostic experiments introduce parsing-failure and erroneous non-zero prediction metrics. Existing benchmark splits and counting metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices P, Q, and S substantially extend diagnostics by measuring parsing failures, comparing prompts with and without zero-count instructions, and evaluating two-axis division. Existing component and crowded-scene analyses remain. v3's small-number-bias analysis and accompanying TallyQA/VQAv2 distributions are removed.

E5.justification: Table 1 changes the stated trial count for the main experimental tables from three to six. Tables 1–4 newly report 95% confidence intervals for LVLM and LVLM-Count MAEs, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting. The interval calculation procedure is not specified.

E6.justification: MAE/RMSE summaries change across all four main benchmarks. With trial reporting also changed, Table 1 replaces GPT-4o/pipeline MAEs of 25.17/18.09 with 25.57/17.86. New results include TallyQA-Complex MAEs of 2.60/2.28 for GPT-4o/pipeline, parsing and zero-count diagnostics, and two-axis division. Reported GPT-4o pipeline latency changes from 3.03 to 2.56 seconds.

T1.justification: The question/expression formulation, division endpoints, mask-based graph construction, and A* description retain the same mathematics. Neither version presents theoretical guarantees or proofs that are added or revised in v4.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same central claims: training-free counting improvements through object-aware divide-and-conquer, prevention of object splitting, and the Emoji-Count benchmark. Expanded motivation and supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 removes the tentative explanation linking counting errors to small-number bias in training data. Appendix Q adds explanations for the rarity of empty subimages and the mitigating effect of zero-aware prompts. The main limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 substantially expands reproducibility information: scikit-learn MeanShift and bandwidth defaults, mask-processing parameters, parsing/retry code, number-word conversion, zero-aware prompting, and Emoji-Count construction details. It also changes the repository pointer and explicitly states benchmark availability. These disclosures do not establish that the underlying settings were changed.

R1.justification: v4 adds Comaniciu and Meer's mean-shift reference and Pedregosa et al.'s scikit-learn reference, while removing Goyal et al.'s VQAv2 reference with its distribution analysis. It expands discussion of specialized counting models' limitations under distribution shift and complex prompts.

P1.justification: The introduction's motivation and Section 4.2's comparison discussion are expanded, acknowledgments are added, and the appendix organization grows around new material. Most existing prose, the contribution list, and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Main tables expand with confidence-interval columns and specialist-model rows already present in Appendix K; timing tables are restructured. New Tables 20–25 add dataset, diagnostic, implementation, and evaluation displays. The old Figure 24 is replaced by Emoji-Count graphics and a two-axis example in Figures 24–26, and table captions move above tables.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's point estimates and qualitative limitation statements, v4 provides uncertainty reporting, practical implementation details, quantitative failure tests, and real-scene complex-question validation. These improve reproducibility and assessment of the existing approach. The gains are limited by the unspecified confidence-interval calculation and newly inconsistent Qwen2 FSC-147 MAEs in Tables 1 and 14: 34.18 versus 34.48.
